core_obligations: Track a generic point of a component of (g o g')^{-1}(s) and use flatness of g' to place its image as a generic point of a component of g^{-1}(s), then add the two shifts (proof lines 15462-15476).

proof_roadmap: The generic point bookkeeping for the shift c + c' (proof lines 15462-15476).
The composition of pullbacks on cycles and Chow groups (proof lines 15478-15480).
difficulty_reason: For flat morphisms g : S' -> S and g' : S'' -> S' with constants c and c' as in Situation labelled situation-setup-base-change, and X -> S locally of finite type with base changes X' and X'', the lemma asserts that the composite data is again of that form, that g^* and (g')^* compose on cycles to the pullback along g o g', and that the same holds on Chow groups with the map of Lemma labelled lemma-pullback-base-change (statement lines 15437-15460). For the first part the proof takes a generic point s'' of a component of (g o g')^{-1}(s), sets s' = g'(s''), notes that s'' is a generic point of a component of (g')^{-1}(s') and, because g' is flat so generalizations lift by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-base-change-flat, that s' is a generic point of a component of g^{-1}(s); the assumed shifts delta'(s') = delta(s) + c and delta''(s'') = delta'(s') + c' then give delta''(s'') = delta(s) + c + c' (proof lines 15462-15476). For the second part, an integral closed subscheme Z of delta-dimension k has base changes Z' and Z'' with g^*[Z] = [Z']_{k+c} and, by Lemma labelled lemma-pullback-coherent-base-change, (g')^*[Z']_{k+c} = [Z'']_{k+c+c'}, which is exactly the composition statement on cycles and hence on Chow groups (proof lines 15478-15480). Tracking the generic points of the iterated fibres to add the shifts is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
